newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - July 11.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- TIN TIN DAILY -- Nine lawyers promised to help parents of illegal immigrant mainland children sue the government for depriving them of their right of abode in Hong Kong. The Immigration Department refused to reveal deportation plans.

-- A Beijing official said that because Hong Kong and China were now one country, the Hong Kong government had no right to reject people sent by the central government to work in Hong Kong, unless they had commited serious crimes such as smuggling.

-- APPLE DAILY -- A local child patient was suspected of having been infected with the AIDS virus through a blood transfusion. The Hospital Authority said it was an accident and was tracking down the possible blood donors.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Taiwan should be inspired by the success of the "one country, two systems" policy in Hong Kong.
-- MING PAO -- The market was shocked by news that prices at a new residential development of Cheung Kong group would be lower than those for second-hand apartments.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- A Chinese official said red-chip companies should notify the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office of major asset acquisitions. It said the office would decide whether the acquisitions violated China's Hong Kong policies.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Universities faced having to cut entry requirements because of falling standards of English.

-- A World Bank study showed that the Chinese government's attempts to reform its state-owned enterprises had so far been unsuccessful and it had no choice but to reduce the state's involvement to a "passive minority ownership".

-- HONG KONG STANDARD -- For the first time since 1962, Macau casino tycoon Stanley Ho revealed the vast fortune he was making in the Portuguese enclave. His flagship company earned a massive HK$4.63 billion net profit last year.
